newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar says expects Israel at Doha Mideast meeting.
newsitem.headline: Qatar says expects Israel at Doha Mideast meeting.

text.p: Qatar said on Saturday it expected Israel to attend a Middle East and North Africa economic conference in Doha next November which has been in doubt due to a peacemaking crisis.

"It's a purely economic forum and we expect Israel to participate in it...but, as you know, all these things are linked to developments on the political front," said Fawaj al-Attiyah, spokesman at Qatar's foreign ministry.

Business and government leaders of Middle East and North African countries are expected to meet in Doha on November 16 for a three-day economic summit -- the fourth since landmark peace negotiations began in 1991.

Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking was plunged into deep crisis in March when Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and a Moslem militant bomber killed himself and three Israeli women in Tel Aviv.

In April, the Arab League recommended that Arab states stop normalising ties with Israel and restore their economic boycott against the Jewish state. U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross has been shuttling between the sides trying to revive peace talks.

Israel's Maariv daily newspaper said recently that at a meeting last week in Washington of Israeli, Qatari, Jordanian, Palestinian, Moroccan, Tunisian, Egyptian, U.S. and European representatives, it was agreed the conference would take place.

An Israeli official speaking on condition he not be named said earlier this week: "The meeting took place and there was a decision to hold the conference as planned," adding that it was up to Qatar to issue a formal announcement on the issue.

Qatar's Attiyah said: "I am not aware of any such large meeting in Washington...But as far as we are concerned we are going to go ahead with the conference and as of now we expect Israel to attend it."

Qatar and Oman had established trade links with Israel after the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestinians in 1993. But they both said they had frozen ties with Israel following what they consider hardline policies by Netanyahu.
